messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test failure and the current bug report indicate that when initializing a Fraction with a maxDenominator from a double value very close to a simple fraction (e.g., 0.5000000001 close to 1/2), an overflow exception is thrown mistakenly.

Looking at the constructor Fraction(double value, int maxDenominator), it delegates to the private constructor Fraction(double value, double epsilon, int maxDenominator, int maxIterations) with epsilon set to 0 and maxIterations to 100.

Inside this private constructor, the code uses a continued fraction algorithm to approximate the double value by a fraction p/q with denominator < maxDenominator. It iteratively computes convergents p2/q2.

The overflow exception arises when |p2| or |q2| exceed Integer.MAX_VALUE (overflow) at line 212-215. The code comment mentions:

"in maxDenominator mode, if the last fraction was very close to the actual value q2 may overflow in the next iteration; in this case return the last one."

However, currently the code throws the FractionConversionException in that case rather than returning the last valid fraction.

This matches the bug report description: when the value is very close to a simple fraction, the next iteration can cause q2 overflow but is unnecessary since the previous fraction is already a good approximation.

Hence, the bug is that the code throws an exception rather than returning the best fraction as intended when the next iteration overflows the denominator.

The test case tests exactly this: new Fraction(0.5000000001, 10) should return 1/2 without throwing, but current code throws the exception.

Therefore, the root cause is the missing handling to return the last fraction when q2 or p2 overflows, instead of throwing an exception unconditionally.

Recent bug reports are not relevant here since they discuss unrelated functionality and exceptions.

In summary, the issue is at line 212-215 in the private constructor Fraction(double, double, int, int) where overflow is checked but the code throws instead of returning the previous convergent fraction.

The fix should change this to return the fraction represented by p1/q1 rather than throwing when overflow is detected but the approximation is sufficiently close.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

Fraction.Fraction(double, int)
Fraction.Fraction(double, double, int, int)
